title: thermoresponse_paper: code and data to predict the heat-shock response of Trypanosoma brucei genes from their UTRs
description:
Code, input data and a Docker environment that reproduce the ROC analysis "Heat Shock Prediction Up vs Down" in the paper Thermo-sensing and argonaute-dependent transcriptome remodelling in trypanosomes.

Bloodstream-form Trypanosoma brucei cells were grown at 34 °C and 40 °C and measured by DIA proteomics and RNA-seq. Genes significantly higher (Up) or lower (Down) at 40 °C were identified with limma (proteomics) and edgeR with cqn (RNA-seq). The 5′UTR and 3′UTR of each gene were encoded with the DNA language model HyenaDNA (medium-450k, mean embedding), and a random forest evaluated by 3-fold cross-validation predicted Up vs Down from the embeddings.

Contents:

  • data/: proteomics protein-group quantities and limma results; RNA-seq featureCounts tables, GC content and edgeR results; curated TREU927 annotation with UTRs and the TriTrypDB release 68 genome; 5′UTR, CDS and 3′UTR sequences of 6,812 genes and their HyenaDNA embeddings; gene universe. MD5 checksums are included.
  • scripts/: one script per step, from the input tables to the ROC figure, and checks against the published results.
  • upstream/: the DIA-NN search parameters, the MaxLFQ script, the RNA-seq alignment and counting commands, and the RNA-seq sample sheet with FASTQ checksums.
  • Dockerfile and Makefile: make all recomputes every step except the GPU embedding step and checks the results. The ROC figure, its AUCs and every out-of-fold prediction are reproduced exactly.

Code is licensed under MIT; the data in data/ and expected/ under CC BY 4.0. Raw RNA-seq reads are in NCBI SRA (BioProject PRJNA1381115) and proteomics raw files in PRIDE (PXD071951).
